rules.title: Security Deposit Itemization, Return, and Nonrefundable Prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants an itemized statement of deposit deductions, return any undeducted portion of the deposit when they transfer or sell the property, and cannot claim a deposit is 'nonrefundable.' Landlords who act in bad faith regarding deposit retention or demands may owe statutory damages up to twice the deposit amount.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential tenancies with a security deposit under California law.
rules.exemptions: Landlord need not comply with itemization documentation requirements if deductions total $125 or less, or if the tenant signs a valid waiver under specified timing conditions.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”
rules.conflict_note: This chunk reflects the 2025 amendment (AB 414) effective January 1, 2026; a separate chunk of this same statute likely addresses the deposit amount cap itself.
